limitations: Single-request sequential sessions on B50/Ryzen 9950X, approximately 74 GiB host RAM. Other devices and concurrency unmeasured.

The full DeepSeek CPU replay uses the exact earlier 121+128 token Vulkan trace. Historical Vulkan timings were not interleaved with the new CPU run; its older harness lacks DRM and process I/O counters.
The earlier DeepSeek continuation repeats 1. Varied teacher-forced continuations were used for Qwen and the new short DeepSeek matrix; this does not measure free-running generation quality.
Cross-backend logit drift exceeds 1e-5, including 0.057971 on the long DeepSeek comparison; matching greedy choices does not satisfy the logit gate.
Memory samples are taken at batch/token boundaries. Vulkan allocator reservations also capture retained arena capacity; OpenCL/SYCL transient peaks between driver samples may be missed.

Private memory means RssAnon plus VmSwap. File-backed model residency and physical read bytes are reported separately; CPU private memory fluctuated by several MiB; allocator retention was not separately instrumented.
The one-row grouped-projection timing is a compute-cost proxy with different mathematical inputs, not an implemented diagonal grouped projection.
Published matrices use preallocated captures. Later harness revisions add diagnostic metadata and planner fixes; the original Vulkan long reference used the older capture harness.
corrective_changes: Dense-only models keep the expert-device argument on the resolved dense device, preventing SYCL auto CPU placement from failing the Qwen loader validation.
DeepSeek41 Engram tables are host-only in VRAM accounting; its wkv projection stays packed and q/k vectors count as f32.
DeepSeek41 automatic caches require an accelerator consumer, and moving dense to CPU cannot silently create a CPU software cache. Explicit requests remain available.
CPU-only placement tests explicitly select CPU with accelerator features compiled.
